712806.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwr̥̄ḱomt, from earlier *kʷetwr̥-dḱomt (“four-ten”). Cognates include Sanskrit चत्वारिंशत् (catvāriṃśát), Latin quadrāgintā, Old Armenian քառասուն (kʻaṙasun).

712808.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷétwores, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwóres. Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀤𐀵𐀫 (qe-to-ro), Sanskrit चतुर् (catur), Old Armenian չորք (čʻorkʻ), Latin quattuor, and Old English fēower (English four).

712861.t: From τιμωρός (tīmōrós, “avenging, avenger”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix), a contraction of τιμάορος (tīmáoros), from τιμή (tīmḗ, “honour”) + ὁράω (horáō, “to see”).

712865.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷinumi, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey- (“to pay”). Cognate with ποινή (poinḗ), Sanskrit चयते (cáyate) and Avestan 𐬗𐬌𐬐𐬀𐬫𐬀𐬝 (cikayat̰).

712831.t: From Proto-Indo-European *téḱ-sneh₂, from *tetḱ- (“to create, produce”). Cognate with τίκτω (tíktō), τέκτων (téktōn), Sanskrit तक्षति (takṣati), Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬱𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (tašaⁱti), Latin texō, tēla, tignum, Proto-Germanic *þahsuz.

712866.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (“who, what”). Cognates include Latin quis and Hittite 𒆪𒅖 (kuiš).

712849.t: From Proto-Hellenic *títʰēmi, *tétʰēmi, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰé-dʰeh₁-ti, reduplicated present from *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place”). The pay/offer senses are from conflation with δίδωμι (dídōmi) in PIE, see Latin -dō.

712827.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn”). The unaspirated first consonant is due to Grassmann's law.

712839.t: From Proto-Indo-European *teh₂- (“to melt”). Cognates include Latin tābeō, Sanskrit तोयम् (toyam), Old Armenian թանամ (tʻanam, “to wet”) and Old English þawian (English thaw), Proto-Slavic *tajati (Russian та́ять (tájatʹ)).

712898.t: Possibly a cognate of Latin taxus or borrowed from Iranian: compare Persian تخش (taxš, “crossbow”).

712805.t: From Proto-Hellenic *térptis, from Proto-Indo-European *térptis (“fulfillment; satisfaction”); by surface analysis, τέρπω (térpō, “to satisfy”) + -σις (-sĭs).

712867.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷís. Cognates include Latin quis and Hittite [script needed] (kuiš).

712882.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *teḱ-der. Proto-Indo-European *títḱeti Proto-Hellenic *tíktō Ancient Greek τίκτω (tíktō) ▲ Hebrew תוךsl.

712893.t: τέμνω (témnō, “to cut”) + -ος (-os). Hypothetically inherited from Proto-Hellenic *tómos, from Proto-Indo-European *tómh₁-o-s, from *temh₁- (“to cut”).

712899.t: τόξον (tóxon, “bow”) + -της (-tēs, masculine suffix for person concerned with something)

712801.t: From Proto-Indo-European *térmn̥, the same source of Latin terminus (“boundary, limit, end”).

712873.t: A variant form of σοι (soi, “to you”), dative of σύ (sú, “thou”).

712844.t: Traditionally analyzed as τηρός (tērós, “a guard”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix), though Beekes considers τηρέω (tēréō) as the original formation and τηρός (tērós) as a back-formation.

712871.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *terh₃- (“to hurt”), with inchoative suffix -σκω (-skō).

712876.t: The base of the Proto-Indo-European demonstrative *tód + the adjective suffix *-yós, equivalent to τό (tó, “this”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

712877.t: From τοῖος (toîos, “such”) + -δε (-de, deictic suffix). Compare ὅδε (hóde, “this here”).

712804.t: From Proto-Hellenic *térpō, from Proto-Indo-European *terp- (“to satisfy”), cognate with German dürfen (“to need”) and obsolete and dialectal British English tharf (“to need”).

712879.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tóikʰos, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeyǵʰ- (“to knead, form, fashion”). Compare τεῖχος (teîkhos), which it appears to be variant of.

712826.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téukʰō, a thematicized formation from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéwgʰti, root present of *dʰewgʰ-.

712846.t: Oriental foreign word of unknown origin.

712884.t: From Proto-Indo-European *telh₂- (“to bear”), like τελαμών (telamṓn, “strap, belt”) and τάλαντον (tálanton, “balance, scale”).

712889.t: Maurice connects τυλυφάντης (tuluphántēs, “cushion-cover weaver”), assuming influence of κορύνη (korúnē) or τορύνη (torúnē) to account for the vocalism. Furnée compares Luwian [script needed] (taluppi, “clump of dough”).

712854.t: Unknown. This verb cannot be an old primary formation.

712814.t: From a reduplicated form of Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- + -αίνω (-aínō).

712896.t: From τόξον (tóxon) + -εύω (-eúō), possibly from Iranian. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀵𐀒𐀰𐀲 (to-ko-so-ta) (archer).

712818.t: From τετρακοσιοστός (tetrăkosĭostós, “four hundred”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).
